title: China-to-Nigeria Industrial Motor Compliance Gap Matrix
provenance: AI-compiled, multi-model cross-checked, not human-verified. Informational only; confirm with the official regulator and a qualified professional. Not legal/certification/customs/market-access advice.

rows.target_requirement: Industrial three-phase AC motors imported into Nigeria are generally assessed through SON conformity controls when they fall in a regulated product category. Nigeria commonly uses Nigerian Industrial Standards that adopt or align with IEC and BS standards; NIS 50034 is the local adoption basis for rotating electrical machines under IEC 60034.
rows.china_equivalent: China industrial motor documentation commonly cites GB 18613 for IE efficiency classes aligned with IEC 60034-30-1, GB 12665 for cooling and related construction references, and CCC where low-voltage motors fall within the CCC catalogue.
rows.gap: A China GB or CCC file set does not establish that the motor is in the correct Nigeria regulated category or that it has been reviewed against the applicable NIS adoption of IEC 60034. The importer should map model ratings, duty, enclosure, insulation, and nameplate data to the Nigeria NIS basis before shipment.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory where the motor is in a SON regulated category and subject to MANCAP import controls
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory where GB 18613, CCC catalogue, or other China compulsory requirements apply

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Treat Nigeria scope classification as a separate SON and NIS exercise. China GB 18613, GB 12665, or CCC evidence may help the technical file but does not replace Nigeria classification or MANCAP review.

rows.target_requirement: Nigeria industrial supply is commonly 415/240 V, 50 Hz. The frequency matches China at 50 Hz, but three-phase line voltage is commonly 415 V rather than China 380 V, so rated voltage, permissible voltage tolerance, thermal rise, torque, current, and service factor should be checked for the Nigeria supply system.
rows.china_equivalent: China motor nameplates and test files commonly assume 380 V three-phase, 50 Hz for standard industrial motors, with efficiency evidence under GB 18613 and related construction references under GB 12665.
rows.gap: A 380 V China motor may operate on 415 V only if its design, insulation, temperature rise, overload, and nameplate tolerance support that service. Nigeria files should not assume voltage equivalence merely because both markets use 50 Hz.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory technical suitability issue under SON and NIS review for Nigeria supply conditions
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory or baseline depending on China motor category, GB 18613 applicability, and CCC catalogue scope

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Confirm 415 V 50 Hz suitability explicitly in the Nigeria technical file. A China 380 V 50 Hz rating is close but not automatically interchangeable for SON or end-user acceptance.

rows.target_requirement: Nigeria energy-efficiency policy for electric motors is developing under the national energy-efficiency direction led by energy authorities such as NAEME and the Federal Ministry of Energy. For industrial AC motors, IE class evidence should be prepared against IEC 60034-30-1 style efficiency classes and the Nigeria NIS adoption basis where requested.
target_standards: Federal Ministry of Energy policy direction
rows.china_equivalent: China uses GB 18613 for motor energy-efficiency limits and IE classes aligned with IEC 60034-30-1 naming, with GB 12665 and CCC baseline documentation depending on the motor configuration and catalogue scope.
rows.gap: China GB 18613 IE evidence is useful but should be translated into a Nigeria-facing IE class statement with test conditions, rated voltage, and frequency clearly shown. Nigeria may ask for evidence that the motor class supports national efficiency policy rather than only a China domestic grade.

mandatory_status.target: Developing policy and potentially mandatory when tied to SON, procurement, or energy-efficiency programme requirements

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Prepare an IE-class package for Nigeria even when the shipment already has China GB 18613 evidence. The Nigeria file should show the applicable IE class, method, voltage, frequency, and rating basis.

rows.target_requirement: For Nigeria review, efficiency claims should be supported by test reports that identify the motor model, rating, pole count, duty, test method, and supply conditions. Where Nigeria applies NIS IEC 60034 expectations, IEC 60034-2-1 style loss and efficiency determination evidence is the practical reference.
rows.china_equivalent: China files commonly include GB 18613 efficiency declarations and China laboratory reports using domestic test methods, with GB 12665 and CCC files as supporting baseline documents when applicable.
rows.gap: Nigeria-facing evidence should not rely only on a China domestic grade label. The file should explain how the China test report maps to the IEC or NIS method, especially if the motor will be operated at 415 V rather than 380 V.

mandatory_status.target: Expected technical evidence when energy performance, SON review, or procurement specifications request IE performance

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Use China test evidence as input, not as a final Nigeria conclusion. A Nigeria dossier should show IEC or NIS mapping and 415 V operating relevance before relying on the efficiency claim.

rows.target_requirement: Nigeria industrial buyers, utilities, and public projects may specify IE2, IE3, or higher motor classes as a commercial or procurement condition even where the regulatory route is through SON MANCAP. Claims should be supported by model-specific test evidence and nameplate marking.
rows.china_equivalent: China exporters often present GB 18613 grade evidence and CCC or GB 12665 technical files as the common China compliance baseline for low-voltage industrial motors.
rows.gap: Procurement specifications may be stricter than the minimum import-control check. A motor that can clear MANCAP documentation may still fail the buyer requirement if the quoted IE class, test method, voltage, or nameplate data do not match the project specification.

mandatory_status.target: Commercially mandatory when written into Nigeria buyer, tender, or project specifications
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory where GB 18613 applies; otherwise baseline evidence for China-origin claims

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Check the Nigeria buyer specification separately from import clearance. Align the IE class, voltage, frequency, and nameplate data with the tender or purchase order before quoting.

rows.target_requirement: Plain industrial motors may have limited standalone EMC emissions, but motor systems with drives, controls, inverters, starters, sensors, or electronic protection can trigger EMC review under SON conformity assessment and applicable NIS or IEC-based standards.
target_standards: NIS standards adopting IEC or BS EMC standards
rows.china_equivalent: China baseline files may include GB 18613 efficiency documents, GB 12665 motor construction references, and CCC documents where low-voltage motor or associated electrical equipment is in scope; EMC evidence may be separate for drives and controllers.
rows.gap: A motor-only China certificate may not cover the EMC behavior of a complete Nigeria shipment that includes a variable-speed drive or electronic starter. The product configuration submitted to SON should match the actual shipped system.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory where SON review or applicable Nigeria-adopted standards cover the electronic motor system
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory only where China CCC or applicable China EMC requirements cover the motor-associated equipment

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Separate the bare motor from the complete motor-control package. Nigeria documentation should include EMC evidence for drives and controllers when those items are shipped with or marketed as part of the system.

rows.target_requirement: If a motor package includes wireless monitoring, telemetry, Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, cellular, or other radio equipment, Nigerian Communications Commission approval may be required in addition to SON import conformity controls.
rows.china_equivalent: China motor documentation under GB 18613, GB 12665, and CCC does not by itself cover Nigeria radio type approval. China SRRC or CCC evidence for wireless modules may be useful support but is not the Nigeria approval.
rows.gap: A smart motor or drive with radio connectivity can require a second Nigeria regulatory path through NCC. The importer should split the motor safety and performance file from the radio-module approval file.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory when radio equipment is included and falls under NCC approval scope
mandatory_status.cn: Not a substitute; China radio or CCC evidence is separate from Nigeria NCC approval

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Check NCC separately whenever the motor package has wireless functionality. SON MANCAP and China CCC evidence do not automatically clear Nigeria radio approval.

rows.target_requirement: Nigeria requires SON MANCAP conformity assessment for listed regulated products before import and market placement. For industrial AC motors in scope, the importer should obtain the required MANCAP certificate or product conformity evidence accepted by SON before shipment or customs clearance.
rows.china_equivalent: China CCC, GB 18613 efficiency evidence, GB 12665 documents, and IEC 60034-30-1 aligned IE-class statements form the common China compliance package but are not Nigeria import certificates.
rows.gap: CCC is not recognized as a substitute for SON MANCAP. China certificates can support the technical review, but the Nigeria importer still needs the SON-recognized import conformity route.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory for listed products under SON MANCAP import controls
mandatory_status.cn: China CCC may be mandatory domestically for catalogue products but is not accepted as Nigeria MANCAP

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Build the shipment plan around SON MANCAP first. China CCC, GB 18613, and GB 12665 evidence may reduce technical friction but do not replace the Nigeria certificate.

rows.target_requirement: NAFDAC regulates food, drugs, cosmetics, medical devices, chemicals, detergents, packaged water, and related regulated goods. Industrial AC motors are not typically NAFDAC-regulated unless supplied as part of a NAFDAC-controlled product, production line, chemical package, or regulated appliance context.
rows.china_equivalent: China motor files typically rely on GB 18613, IEC 60034-30-1 alignment, GB 12665, and CCC where applicable; these do not address Nigeria NAFDAC classification.
rows.gap: For ordinary industrial motors, the practical Nigeria path is usually SON rather than NAFDAC. However, if the motor is imported with regulated chemicals, medical equipment, food equipment, or a controlled production system, NAFDAC questions may arise at the package level.

mandatory_status.target: Usually not applicable to standalone industrial motors; mandatory only if the shipment falls within NAFDAC-regulated goods or systems
mandatory_status.cn: No China motor equivalent; CCC and GB evidence do not answer Nigeria NAFDAC scope

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Do not route a standalone industrial motor through NAFDAC by default. Check NAFDAC only when the motor is bundled with goods or systems that NAFDAC regulates.

source.publisher: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control

rows.target_requirement: Nigeria enforcement has been improving after post-2020 border and import-control reforms. Importers should prepare SON MANCAP evidence, invoice, packing list, model list, test reports, and standards mapping before shipment rather than relying on document remediation after arrival.
rows.china_equivalent: China-origin files may include GB 18613, IEC 60034-30-1 aligned IE-class evidence, GB 12665 documents, and CCC records, but these should be organized into a Nigeria customs and SON submission set.
rows.gap: Late documentation increases detention, rework, and demurrage risk. The China file set should be converted into a Nigeria import packet before booking shipment, with model numbers and HS descriptions matching the commercial documents.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory operational requirement for regulated imports subject to SON and customs checks
mandatory_status.cn: China evidence supports but does not replace Nigeria border documentation

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Prepare the MANCAP and customs packet before shipment. A China CCC or GB file set that is not mapped to Nigeria documents can still cause border delay.

rows.target_requirement: Nigeria SON review for industrial motors should cover electrical and mechanical safety issues under NIS standards that adopt IEC 60034 principles, including insulation class, temperature rise, ingress protection, earthing, terminal box design, rotating part protection, and nameplate markings.
rows.china_equivalent: China motor safety and construction files commonly cite GB 12665, GB 18613 for efficiency, IEC 60034-30-1 aligned IE classes, and CCC where the motor falls within the low-voltage CCC baseline.
rows.gap: China safety evidence should be checked against Nigeria NIS and actual Nigeria installation conditions. The 415 V supply, ambient conditions, enclosure protection, cable entries, and earthing arrangements can affect acceptance even if the China design file is complete.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory where SON MANCAP or Nigeria-adopted NIS motor safety requirements apply
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory where applicable China GB or CCC requirements apply

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Review safety at the motor and installation level for Nigeria. China GB 12665 or CCC evidence should be mapped to NIS IEC 60034 expectations and local 415 V use.

rows.target_requirement: Motors intended for petroleum, gas, mining, dust, chemical, or other hazardous locations in Nigeria may require additional explosion-protection, enclosure, certification, and end-user acceptance evidence beyond ordinary SON MANCAP motor review.
target_standards: NIS standards adopting IEC hazardous-area standards
rows.china_equivalent: China ordinary motor documents under GB 18613, GB 12665, IEC 60034-30-1 alignment, and CCC do not prove hazardous-area suitability. China explosion-protection certificates, if any, should be treated as separate supporting evidence.
rows.gap: A general-purpose industrial motor file is insufficient for hazardous areas. The Nigeria dossier should identify the zone, gas or dust group, temperature class, enclosure method, and accepted certification route before shipment.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory when the intended Nigeria installation is a hazardous or special regulated environment
mandatory_status.cn: China ordinary motor compliance is not enough; separate hazardous-area evidence is needed where applicable

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Do not reuse an ordinary China motor dossier for Nigeria hazardous-area service. Confirm IEC 60079-style evidence and local acceptance route before shipment.
